next_question: On a substrate that imposes genuine cold-discovery cost -- multi-step auth, pagination and schema discovery, such that the B-COLD no-memory baseline provably costs more than one request per task and the amortization comparison has dynamic range -- does the now-durable kernel distill_parameterized reach amortized_cost_ratio <= 0.85 against B-COLD, B-LITERAL-REPLAY and B-RETRIEVAL-K5 at matched end-to-end success and break even within a preregistered number of transfer tasks rather than the 253.8 measured here, while abstaining with false_accept_rate <= 0.10 when a slot is bound outside the observed support, under thresholds derived from that substrate's measured baseline cost and frozen before any arm runs?
why_next: This packet closed the program's first real mechanism question and left exactly one of its two halves unmeasured. D1, D2, D3, D4 and D7 all passed on a real, reachable, self-tested HTTP substrate with a durable committed kernel capability and all three preregistered baselines at mechanism_success_rate 0.0, so re-asking whether mechanisms can parameterize to never-observed identifiers here would only re-derive a known result. The compound rule nevertheless returned FAIL (FALSIFIES) on D5 and the D6 cost half, and the independent audit showed both thresholds are unreachable for any system on this substrate because cold exploration already costs 1.0 HTTP request per read and per query. The falsifying conditions therefore fired without identifying the proposition they were written to identify, which leaves exactly one high-information, decidable question: does the same committed mechanism amortize its induction cost where the baseline actually has a cost to amortize against, and does it abstain in the failure direction that this run never probed. Fixing the substrate and the threshold derivation converts an unbounded sequence of blocked or degenerate packets into a decidable economic measurement, and the answer is the one that decides whether the accumulating architecture is worth building at all.

established: A durable, committed, unit-tested parameter-induction capability now exists in the product kernel rather than in a harness: spider.kernel.distill_parameterized(observations), SpiderKernel.distill_parameterized(observations, register=True) and align_parameters in src/spider/kernel.py (sha256 ac1cbdd92342d32369f4dcdbe3e58ce688c07d2690f252b66bfb3c84212f6501), re-exported from src/spider/__init__.py, committed at 664bc124, exercised by 20/20 passing tests (tests/test_kernel.py sha256 efcd6649b2379ec2e2327adad635cbecbec251c830aeaad591a839033ce627e9; artifacts/raw/unit_tests.txt sha256 39f1cbcff3f9c9c17ce77bd215c34a8fdb65a720bf39ece793d02b5c649d6bf3). This closes the specific defect the Codex recorded for EXP-GRAPH-36118890504, 'no durable kernel distill_parameterized capability', where induction was a harness substitute.

On this substrate, mechanisms induced from 100 successful resource-A observations bind correctly to never-observed resource-B identifiers whose value set is disjoint (products SKU-A..SKU-Z and PROD-100..199 vs items/tags item-N/tag-N; provenance fixtures.substrate.identifier_overlap_a_b = []): mechanism success 1.0 in all three families (crud-write, crud-read, query), binding accuracy 1.0, kernel verification 1.0, 0 cold fallbacks, 1.0 HTTP request per task, amortized 1.0 (audit.json recomputed_metrics treatment_* and result.json metrics). This is the audited ceiling; it is not population-level generalization.

Induced confidence is evidence-derived rather than hardcoded: 0.956522 = Beta(2,1) posterior mean x leave-one-out re-construction consistency 1.0 across the 5 induced mechanisms (artifacts/raw/induced_mechanisms.json sha256 dda76d9988d96a7a00e5e62918f88a7cff86423a624dca81fe44ea8106ffbb2a), which clears min_confidence=0.8 and therefore returns EXECUTABLE through the ordinary resolve() path. The 'kernel cannot execute anything it learns' defect is closed for the parameterized path only.

Abstention on this substrate: 60 negative probes per arm (40 unlearned-intent probes over 2 collections and 2 roles, plus 20 prefix-collision probes) all resolved UNKNOWN with 0 false accepts, giving abstention_precision 1.0 and false_accept_rate 0.0 (artifacts/raw/negative_probes.json sha256 954c8c5db504c9994bcc1dbc7f953937d39a5c390f46006a72e57ca2ac4d734d).

The null control NC-SHUFFLED-INTENT transfers at mechanism_success_rate 0.0 with abstention_precision 1.0 and cost ratio 1.0, so the treatment's transfer is carried by genuine intent structure rather than a permissive pattern matcher (artifacts/raw/arm_NC-SHUFFLED-INTENT.json sha256 181279c432b6dbd48c037af6e0791812fc81cfa7134fd6b253b955a99f86bb7a).

All three preregistered baselines recorded mechanism_success_rate 0.0 (B-COLD, B-LITERAL-REPLAY, B-RETRIEVAL-K5) and reached end-to-end success 1.0 only through cold fallback; B-COLD was correctly selected as the best baseline at matched correctness under a competence floor of 0.80 and a 0.05 tolerance, both of which make the D5 test harder for the treatment. B-COLD is a strong baseline here, not a strawman: 1.0 HTTP request per read and per query task because its first generic REST candidate matches this substrate's API.

Incumbent reference curve, measured on the committed kernel exactly as committed, matches the prereg expectation precisely: no distill_parameterized, distill confidence 0.5 against min_confidence 0.8, same-intent resolution EXPLORE 'candidate exists but confidence is below execution threshold', paraphrased intent UNKNOWN 'no applicable validated mechanism', 0.0 EXECUTABLE on the resource-B probe with 0 HTTP requests, and applicability_guards, failure_boundary, freshness, repair_scope and verification_rule all observed empty (artifacts/raw/incumbent_reference_curve.json sha256 dbeddf9653aade3266d555d56da030cf83f700767b84f224b2e0bf7a71a74e7a).

Three real product-code defects were found by running the experiment and fixed under unit tests: string-only slot alignment that could not represent integer-valued query parameters (unfixed, it drove the list-intent confidence to 0 and would have been published as a 0.0 scientific result), verbatim copying of a constant Authorization header into a durable template (the parameterized path now stores ${auth_token}), and volatile session metadata promoted to a hard precondition (now filtered by the same denylist).

The decision-relevant decomposition of the frozen gate is established and is not in dispute: D1, D2, D3, D4 and D7 pass; D5 (amortized cost ratio 1.01626 crud-write, 1.66667 crud-read, 1.66667 query against 0.85) and the D6 cost half (2.0 against 0.50) fail; measured break-even is 253.8 transfer tasks on crud-write and never reached on crud-read or query (artifacts/derived/decision_rule.json sha256 e2ece1d82ed2303f18133ef86905397b85a26c3adf1a75f8bb3083886d7b9345).
rejected: Bounded to this substrate and task construction: literal replay of a resource-A mechanism does not transfer to resource-B identifiers. B-LITERAL-REPLAY recorded mechanism_success_rate 0.0, and B-LITERAL-REPLAY-FORCED, given a valid working credential to isolate identifier transfer from authorization, still recorded binding_accuracy 0.0 and mechanism_success_rate 0.0. Only the parameter-slot path transferred.

Bounded to this substrate and task construction: top-5 semantic retrieval with heuristic slot matching also failed to transfer (B-RETRIEVAL-K5 and the B-RETRIEVAL-K5-SLOT diagnostic both mechanism_success_rate 0.0). This does NOT establish that retrieval is a weak baseline in general; Intel and Frontier own verified external baselines, and this comparison is a local harness comparison only.

Bounded: the prereg section 9 falsifier's economic trigger did fire and the frozen compound rule did return FAIL (FALSIFIES); that record stands and must not be erased. What is rejected is the inference the prereg section 10 attached to it -- that parameterized inheritance is FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING as SPIDER's central mechanism and the architecture must change to non-inheriting alternatives. audit.json validity_findings show both failing thresholds have zero dynamic range on this substrate for any system including a correct one, so this measurement cannot identify that conclusion in either direction.

Bounded: the D6 positive-control cost criterion (cost_ratio <= 0.50 vs B-COLD) is non-discriminating on this substrate, because B-COLD also costs 1.0 request per task on the positive-control task set. The control's substantive halves pass (mechanism success 1.0, binding accuracy 1.0 over 100 held-out resource-A tasks). No substitute threshold was substituted post hoc.

Rejected as an explanation of the observed transfer: spurious pattern matching without intent structure. NC-SHUFFLED-INTENT transfers at 0.0 with abstention 1.0, so the treatment's 1.0 is not a permissive-matcher artifact.

Rejected as a substrate: the prior Graph packet EXP-GRAPH-36118890504 remains a measurement-invalid record about inherited mechanisms and must not be cited as evidence that inheritance fails; this packet re-measured the capability from scratch on a reachable substrate and provenance records that its negative-sounding wording was explicitly not inherited.
unknown: Whether parameterized inheritance is economically viable at all, i.e. whether the D5 failure is intrinsic to the mechanism or an artifact of this substrate's near-zero cold-baseline cost. Unresolved by design of the audit; separating the two requires a substrate with genuine discovery cost.
Whether the amortization and positive-control cost thresholds can ever be made discriminating without a different substrate, and what pre-freeze derivation from measured baseline cost makes them so.

Whether the mechanism abstains correctly when a slot is bound outside the observed support. This run shows it does not abstain and does succeed on a third collection value (products, when only items and tags were observed); the failure direction is untested, and the measured false_accept_rate 0.0 comes from unlearned-intent and prefix-collision probes, not from out-of-support slot bindings.

Whether the same machinery spans schemas with different field names, nested request bodies or multi-step flows. Induced slots covered only collection, id, q, limit and auth_token, i.e. a single collection dimension.

Freshness and staleness (C-FRESHNESS) were not exercised. The mechanisms' freshness fields hold evidence-scope metadata (observed_distinct_identifiers 20 for CRUD intents and 2 for list, observed_sessions 1, observed_conditional_get false), which is not a staleness decision.

Repair on binding or execution failure (C-DELTA-REPAIR) is unmeasured. The induced mechanisms record repair_scope policy 'none' with the note that delta repair is out of scope, and the fallback exercised in this run is harness-level cold exploration, not a kernel repair capability.
Population-level generalization beyond these 150 task constructions. Per-family counts are exact out of 50 and the family-stratified bootstrap CI (B=5000) is degenerate at [1.0, 1.0].

Whether the two open product defects will be fixed and what that would do to the incumbent reference curve: the literal SpiderKernel.distill() path still hardcodes confidence 0.5 against min_confidence 0.8, and literal mechanisms still persist the resource-A Authorization bearer token in a durable action_template.

do_not_assume: Do not assume C-PARAM-INHERIT is validated or promoted. Its status is EXPERIMENTAL (bounded), promote_to_product is false, and the product capability is retained-but-unpromoted. SHIPPED does not apply to this packet.

Do not assume the prereg's architecture-pivot conclusion in either direction. The compound FALSIFIES label is real and must remain on the record; its causal content (inheritance is economically wrong, so move to non-inheriting alternatives) is NOT identified by this measurement, because the two failing thresholds were unreachable for any system on this substrate. Equally, do not read success_rate 1.0 as evidence that the mechanism is economically viable.

Do not read 1.0 HTTP request per task as a product economics result. It is one stdlib REST substrate where cold exploration is already about 1 request. Model tokens, browser and network egress, real-agent success, latency amortization and maintenance cost are all unmeasured here, and C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS.

Do not read the substrate as Flask. prereg sections 2 and 8 named Flask; the environment had none, so the substrate is stdlib http.server on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port, verified by self-test before any arm ran, and disclosed in validity_notes.
Do not treat the collection-slot transfer as interpolation. Only items and tags were ever observed, so binding products is out-of-support extrapolation to a third value of that slot.

Do not interpret treatment ECE 0.0435 as evidence of calibration quality. All 150 treatment resolutions emit the single confidence 0.956522, so it is a one-bin quantity; the pooled all-arm ECE 0.0198 over n=550 is the more informative number and it pools all arms, not just the treatment.

Do not assume durable templates are credential-safe in general. The parameterized path stores ${auth_token} and no live credential appears in any treatment artifact, but the literal incumbent distill() path still persists the resource-A bearer token in action_template (artifacts/raw/literal_mechanisms.json).
Do not assume the kernel can execute everything it learns. Only the parameterized path produces confidence above min_confidence 0.8; literal mechanisms still resolve to EXPLORE or UNKNOWN.

Do not treat a low success rate as a scientific result without checking the integer-slot defect class first. Unfixed string-only slot alignment silently produced a 0.0 success rate on the query family that would have been reported as evidence against inheritance; any re-run on a new substrate must re-verify binding of non-string parameter types.
Do not treat harness-level cold exploration as a product capability. Every baseline end-to-end success of 1.0 was achieved by falling back to cold exploration, not by inheritance.

Do not treat this bounded result as closing parameterized inheritance, the inheritance architecture, or the Product lane. A bounded negative on this substrate's economics does not terminate the claim, and the domain remains open.

Do not assume the next experiment is authorized. A new product packet on a different substrate is a NEW experiment requiring a Global Research Director mandate; lanes do not self-authorize child experiments, and this handoff's next_question is a proposal, not a dispatch.

recommended_action: Do not promote and do not re-run this substrate. Route the next_question in this handoff to the Global Research Director as the highest-information product question, and keep the committed kernel capability at EXPERIMENTAL and unpromoted until a discriminating economic measurement exists. For that next product packet, require that the substrate be built and its cold-baseline cost measured BEFORE freeze so the amortization and positive-control cost thresholds are derived from measured dynamic range rather than assumed constants -- D5 and D6 were unreachable for any system here, including a correct one, and that is the specific design defect that produced a FALSIFIES label with no information content. Avoid further all-or-nothing compound gates in which one non-discriminating condition can void an otherwise decisive mechanism result; report mechanism and economics as separately decidable gates. Keep the two open product defects (literal distill confidence 0.5 below min_confidence 0.8, and credential persistence in the literal template) explicitly tracked, and do not close them by assertion.
